'''Theodore Lawrence Brown''' (October 15, 1928 – March 24, 2026) was an American scientist known for research, teaching, and writing in the field of [[physical inorganic chemistry]], a university administrator, and a philosopher of science.<ref name=Laszlo>{{cite journal|last1=Laszlo|first1=Pierre|title=Metaphors Chemists Live By|journal=Hyle: International Journal for Philosophy of Chemistry|date=2004|volume=10|issue=1|pages=47–51|url=http://www.hyle.org/journal/issues/10-1/ess_laszlo.htm|accessdate=5 September 2015}}</ref> In addition to his research publications, Brown has written textbooks on [[general chemistry]] and [[science communication]] which have been published in multiple languages and used in multiple countries. He was a professor emeritus at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], where he has also held the administrative positions of vice chancellor for research and dean of the graduate college (1980–1986). He was the founding director emeritus of the [[Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology]]. He died at home on March 24, 2026, after a brief illness.<ref>[https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/news-gazette/name/theodore-ted-lawrence-brown-obituary?id=61114877 Theodore (Ted) Lawrence Brown], legacy.com.</ref>

==Life and career==
Theodore L. Brown was born in [[Green Bay, Wisconsin]] October 15, 1928, to Lawrence A. Brown and Martha E. (Kedinger) Brown.<ref name=Evory/> He earned a Bachelor of Science in chemistry at the [[Illinois Institute of Technology]] in 1950.   From 1950 to 1953, he served with the [[United States Navy|U.S. Navy]].<ref name=Atwood/> On January 6, 1951, he married Audrey Catherine Brockman.<ref name=Evory>{{cite book|last1=Evory|first1=Ann|title=Contemporary authors : a bio-bibliographical guide to current writers in fiction, general nonfiction, poetry, journalism, drama, motion pictures, television, and other fields.|url=https://archive.org/details/contemporaryauth29-32anne|url-access=registration|date=1978|publisher=Gale Research|location=Gale Research|isbn=978-0810300385|edition=1. rev.}}</ref><ref name=FamilySearch>{{cite web|title=Indiana Marriages, 1811-200, database with images, Theodore L. Brown and Audrey Brockman, 1951|url=https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XXNH-RMW|website=FamilySearch|accessdate=4 September 2015}}</ref>

Brown then attended [[Michigan State University]],<ref name=ChemistryIllinois>{{cite web|title=Theodore L. Brown Emeritus Professor of Chemistry|url=http://www.chemistry.illinois.edu/faculty/theodore_brown.html|website=Chemistry at Illinois|accessdate=4 September 2015|quote= A number of sources, including some at Illinois, incorrectly give his alma mater as the University of Michigan.}}</ref> where he worked with [[Max T. Rogers]]. He was a Du Pont Teaching Fellow, 1955–1956.<ref name=Brown1957>{{cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=Theodore L.|last2=Rogers|first2=Max T.|title=The Preparation and Properties of Crystalline Lithium Alkyls|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|date=April 1957|volume=79|issue=8|pages=1859–1861|doi=10.1021/ja01565a024|bibcode=1957JAChS..79.1859B }}</ref>   He received his Ph.D. in 1956. His thesis, ''I. Solution Structures of Lithium Alkyl Compounds. II. Infrared Intensities of the OH Stretching Bond in Alcohols'', identified two research areas that he would focus on early in his career.<ref name=Atwood>{{cite journal|last1=Atwood|first1=Jim D.|title=DEDICATION|journal=Journal of Coordination Chemistry|date=June 1994|volume=32|issue=1–3|pages=i–ii|doi=10.1080/00958979408024232}}</ref>

He joined the faculty of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], where he became an assistant professor of chemistry in 1958, an associate professor in 1961, and a professor in 1965.<ref name=IllinoisArchives/> His textbook ''Chemistry: The Central Science'', initially coauthored with H. E. LeMay, has been published in fourteen editions.<ref name=ChemistryIllinois/>  Between 1958 and 1993, when he retired from teaching, Brown supervised 61 Ph.D. students and 28 postdoctoral scholars.<ref name=Atwood/> As of 1994 he became professor emeritus of chemistry at the University of Illinois.<ref name=Committee/>

Brown published extensively on [[alkyl lithium reagent]]s in solution in the 1960s.  His work in the 1970s includes contributions on [[Metal carbonyl|metal carbonyl complexes]], metal carbonyl radicals, [[molecular orbital theory]], and [[Nuclear quadrupole resonance]].<ref name=Atwood/> He has researched and published extensively in the areas of inorganic chemistry, [[organometallic chemistry]], [[chemical kinetics]] and mechanisms of reactions.<ref name=Committee/>

He served as the vice-chancellor for research and dean of the graduate college from 1980 to 1986.<ref name=ChemistryIllinois/>  He was the founding director emeritus of the [[Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology]], University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, which he headed from 1987 to 1993.<ref name=IllinoisArchives>{{cite web|title=Theodore L. Brown Papers, 1951–1996|url=http://archives.library.illinois.edu/archon/?p=collections/controlcard&id=4655|website=University of Illinois Archives|accessdate=4 September 2015}}</ref> Brown's book ''Bridging divides'' describes the development of the institute.<ref name=Brown2009>{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Theodore L.|title=Bridging divides : the origins of the Beckman Institute at Illinois|date=2009|publisher=University of Illinois|location=Urbana|isbn=978-0252034848|url=http://www.press.uillinois.edu/books/catalog/38tnd6hm9780252034848.html|accessdate=11 December 2014}}</ref><ref name="hundred">{{cite book | isbn = 978-0-941901-23-9 |author1=Arnold Thackray  |author2=Minor Myers, Jr. |name-list-style=amp |others = foreword by James D. Watson. | year = 2000 | publisher = Chemical Heritage Foundation | location = Philadelphia, Pa. | title = Arnold O. Beckman : one hundred years of excellence}}</ref> Brown also served as a council member of the Government-University-Industry Research Roundtable during 1989–1994.<ref name=Roundtable>{{cite book | author=National Academy of Sciences | author2=National Academy of Engineering | author3=Institute of Medicine | title=Facilitating interdisciplinary research | publisher=National Academies Press | publication-place=Washington, D.C. | date=2005 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zJMrAAAAYAAJ&pg=PR5 | isbn=978-0-309-54727-7 | oclc=70737622 | page=5}}</ref> He also co-chaired a National Academies committee on Facilitating Interdisciplinary Research for the Committee on Science, Engineering and Public Policy (2003-2005).<ref name=ChemistryIllinois/><ref name=Committee/> He served on the board of directors of the Arnold and Mabel Beckman Foundation during 1994–2008.

Brown's later work focuses on the cognitive, philosophical and social aspects of science. In 2003 he published the widely cited ''Making Truth: Metaphor in Science'', exploring metaphorical reasoning in science.<ref name=Laszlo/><ref name=Sardella>{{cite journal|last1=Sardella|first1=D. J.|title=Review of Making Truth. Metaphor In Science, by Theodore L. Brown|journal=The Nucleus|date=2004|volume=February|url=https://www.academia.edu/7112039|accessdate=10 September 2015}}</ref> ''Imperfect Oracle: The Epistemic and Moral Authority of Science in Society'', appeared in 2009.<ref name=ChemistryIllinois/> In 2018 he published a work of historical fiction, "''The Beauty of their Dreams''".

Brown died on March 24, 2026, at the age of 97.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remembering Theodore “Ted” Brown, the founding director of the Beckman Institute |url=https://beckman.illinois.edu/news/article/2026/03/27/remembering-theodore--ted--brown--the-founding-director-of-the-beckman-institute |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Default |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Brown was an [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellow]]<ref name=Brown1966>{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Theodore L.|title=Advances in organometallic chemistry.|date=1966|publisher=Elsevier|location=Burlington|isbn=978-0080580043|chapter=The Structures of Organolithium Compounds|pages=365–395|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AHEPoIx22iwC&pg=PA365|accessdate=5 September 2015}}</ref> and a [[National Science Foundation]] Senior Postdoctoral Fellow (1965)<ref name=Brown1966/> and in 1979 was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref name=Guggenheim>{{cite web|title=Theodore L. Brown|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/theodore-l-brown/|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|accessdate=5 September 2015}}</ref> He was honored with the American Chemical Society Award for Research in Inorganic Chemistry in 1972,<ref name=ACSAIOCA>{{cite web|title=ACS Award in Inorganic Chemistry|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/acs-award-in-inorganic-chemistry.html|website=ACS Chemistry for Life|publisher=American Chemical Society|accessdate=3 April 2015}}</ref> and with the American Chemical Society Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Inorganic Chemistry in 1993.<ref name=Award1993>{{cite web|title=ACS Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of lnorganic Chemistry|url=http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/acs-award-for-distinguished-service-in-the-advancement-of-lnorganic-chemistry.html|website=ACS Chemistry for Life|accessdate=5 September 2015}}</ref>  He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in  1987 and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1994.<ref name=Committee>{{cite book | author=National Academy of Sciences | author2=National Academy of Engineering | author3=Institute of Medicine | title=Facilitating interdisciplinary research | publisher=National Academies Press | publication-place=Washington, D.C. | date=2005 | isbn=978-0-309-54727-7 | oclc=70737622 |page=210|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ObxTAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA210}}</ref> He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2010.<ref name=Ahlberg>{{cite news|last1=Ahlberg|first1=Liz|title=Four University of Illinois professors elected ACS fellows|url=https://news.illinois.edu/news/10/0804american_chemical_society_fellows.html|accessdate=5 September 2015|work=University of Illinois News Bureau|date=August 4, 2010}}</ref>
